text:
The story around Matt Rempe right now is ice time, or the lack of it. A New York Post headline on Nov. 1 had him "frustrated" by his playing time with the Rangers: "It's tough." Three days later the Post wrote that he was focused on rare chances "as trade rumor lingers," and Oilers Nation reported Edmonton eyeing the heavyweight. Nothing has happened yet, but it hangs over every shift.

And he hasn't had many. Rempe has dressed five times, out of the lineup between Oct. 13 and Nov. 3, at under 7 minutes a night. He's thrown 22 hits, which tells you the job. The 6-foot-9 Calgary native has no points yet but has held his own: the Rangers get 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him out there, about what they get without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 25% of his entries last season, so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck. Three straight games in the lineup is his longest run this season. Whether that's an audition for New York or for someone else is the question.
headline: Matt Rempe wants to play, and Edmonton is watching
